mentions.heading: Supplier shortages or delays in supply of components
mentions.detail: Prolonged shortage of critical components could disrupt production schedules for key products; fewer sources give suppliers pricing leverage amid OEM price-down pressure
mentions.quote: If we experience a prolonged shortage of critical components from any of our suppliers and cannot procure the components from other sources, we may be unable to meet the production schedules for some of our key products and could miss customer delivery expectations.

mentions.heading: Suppliers' economic distress could result in supply interruptions
mentions.detail: EV adoption volatility, OEM price-down pressure, tariffs and commodity costs strain suppliers; company sometimes provides financial support to distressed suppliers
mentions.quote: In certain instances, it would be difficult and expensive for us to change suppliers that are critical to our business. On occasion, we must provide financial support to distressed suppliers or take other measures to protect our supply lines.

mentions.heading: Possible insolvency of financial counterparties
mentions.detail: Exposure via insurance, letters of credit, credit lines, derivatives and investment management agreements
mentions.quote: We are subject to the risk that one or more of these counterparties may become insolvent and, therefore, be unable to meet its obligations under such contracts.

mentions.heading: Spin-off of PHINIA may not achieve anticipated tax benefits
mentions.detail: PHINIA spin-off intended tax-free for U.S. federal purposes; if taxable, significant income tax liabilities
mentions.quote: If the spin-off is ultimately determined to be taxable, the Company, PHINIA, or the Company’s stockholders could incur income tax liabilities that could be significant.

mentions.heading: Potential liabilities pursuant to the spin-off of PHINIA
mentions.detail: Lawsuit over ~$120 million VAT refunds settled for $78 million; net $40 million charge recorded at December 31, 2025
mentions.quote: On October 15, 2025, the Company entered into a settlement agreement (the “Settlement Agreement”) with PHINIA, pursuant to which PHINIA agreed to pay the Company $78 million, resolving the lawsuit and certain other matters relating to the spin-off.
